name: Secondary Interstitial Lung Disease in Childhood and Adulthood Associated with a Systemic Disease
aliases: Secondary ILD due to Systemic Disorders

criteria.description: Presence of systemic disease with clinical features consistent with connective tissue or systemic inflammatory disorder
High-resolution CT scan showing interstitial lung disease pattern consistent with secondary ILD
Restrictive ventilatory defect and reduced diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO)
Exclusion of idiopathic interstitial pneumonias and other primary lung diseases
Presence of autoantibodies or serologic markers supporting systemic disease diagnosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of systemic disease with compatible clinical features plus radiologic evidence of ILD and pulmonary function abnormalities, excluding primary idiopathic ILD
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including rheumatology and pulmonology input.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic fine bibasilar crackles on auscultation
searchTerms: soft crackling noises when breathing in

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of chronic hypoxia and lung fibrosis

common.notes: Worsening shortness of breath on exertion
searchTerms: worsening shortness of breath with activity

common.notes: Dry cough persisting over weeks to months
Joint pain associated with systemic disease
Generalized tiredness linked to underlying disease

occasional.notes: May be related to inflammatory myopathy

searchTerms: dry eyes and dry mouth symptoms

occasional.notes: May indicate right heart strain secondary to lung disease

searchTerms: symptoms of high lung blood pressure

rare.notes: Seen in systemic sclerosis with severe vascular involvement
Peripheral neuropathy in some systemic diseases

laboratory: Positive autoantibodies (ANA, anti-Scl-70, anti-RNP, anti-CCP depending on systemic disease)
Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
imaging: High-resolution CT showing ground-glass opacities, reticulation, and honeycombing
genetic: No specific genetic markers; familial predisposition may exist in some systemic diseases
other: Pulmonary function tests showing restrictive pattern and reduced DLCO
Bronchoalveolar lavage may show lymphocytosis or neutrophilia depending on underlying disease

distinguishingFeatures: Typical usual interstitial pneumonia pattern on imaging
Presence of granulomas on lung biopsy

redFlags: Signs of acute exacerbation such as new infiltrates and respiratory failure
references: American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society International Multidisciplinary Consensus Classification of the Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias, Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2002
Interstitial lung disease in systemic autoimmune rheumatic disorders, Nat Rev Rheumatol. 2017
Orphanet: Secondary interstitial lung disease in childhood and adulthood associated with a systemic disease, ORPHA:264949
